claim: Ribozyme switches are a class of RNA-encoded genetic switch that support conditional regulation of gene expression across diverse organisms.
source: Ribozyme switches are a class of RNA-encoded genetic switch that support conditional regulation of gene expression across diverse organisms.
evidence: This is a definitional statement about ribozyme switches presented in the abstract, supported by the broader literature context.

claim: A training data set of hundreds of thousands of ribozyme sequences was generated for model development.
source: Here, we generated data on the activity of hundreds of thousands of ribozyme sequences.
evidence: The manuscript describes the experimental generation of this data set through FACS-Seq experiments.

claim: The developed predictive models estimate the in vivo gene-regulatory activity of a ribozyme sequence.
source: Using automated structural analysis and machine learning, we leveraged these large data sets to develop predictive models that estimate the in vivo gene-regulatory activity of a ribozyme sequence.
evidence: The abstract describes the development and function of the models based on the experimental work.

claim: The models supported de novo design of ribozyme libraries with low mean basal gene-regulatory activities.
source: These models supported the de novo design of ribozyme libraries with low mean basal gene-regulatory activities and new ribozyme switches that exhibit changes in gene-regulatory activity in the presence of a target ligand, producing functional switches for four out of five aptamers.
evidence: The abstract reports the experimental outcomes of applying the models to design ribozyme libraries.

claim: Functional switches were produced for four out of five aptamers tested.
source: These models supported the de novo design of ribozyme libraries with low mean basal gene-regulatory activities and new ribozyme switches that exhibit changes in gene-regulatory activity in the presence of a target ligand, producing functional switches for four out of five aptamers.
evidence: The abstract explicitly states the success rate of switch design across different aptamers.

claim: Machine learning can be applied to RNA sequences to predict gene-regulatory activity.
source: Our work examines how biases in the model and the data set that affect prediction accuracy can arise and demonstrates that machine learning can be applied to RNA sequences to predict gene-regulatory activity, providing the basis for design tools for functional RNAs.
evidence: The abstract summarizes the demonstration of machine learning application to RNA sequences.

claim: Genetic switches enable organisms to survive stressful conditions in natural systems.
source: In natural systems, they enable organisms to survive stressful conditions (Oppenheim et al., 2005), and in the hands of genetic engineers, genetic switches have enabled a diverse set of useful applications, from evaluating thousands of biological designs in a single experiment (Michener and Smolke, 2012) to creating safer therapies (Ren et al., 2018).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Oppenheim et al., 2005.

claim: Genetic switches have enabled evaluation of thousands of biological designs in a single experiment.
source: In natural systems, they enable organisms to survive stressful conditions (Oppenheim et al., 2005), and in the hands of genetic engineers, genetic switches have enabled a diverse set of useful applications, from evaluating thousands of biological designs in a single experiment (Michener and Smolke, 2012) to creating safer therapies (Ren et al., 2018).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Michener and Smolke, 2012.

claim: Genetic switches have been used to create safer therapies.
source: In natural systems, they enable organisms to survive stressful conditions (Oppenheim et al., 2005), and in the hands of genetic engineers, genetic switches have enabled a diverse set of useful applications, from evaluating thousands of biological designs in a single experiment (Michener and Smolke, 2012) to creating safer therapies (Ren et al., 2018).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Ren et al., 2018.

claim: RNA switches work through mechanisms including altering transcription termination, transcript stability, and translation initiation.
source: They work through a variety of mechanisms, including altering transcription termination (Fowler et al., 2008), transcript stability (Ausländer et al., 2010), and translation initiation (Klauser et al., 2012).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to three different papers describing different mechanisms.

claim: Ribozyme switches couple the binding of ligand to an RNA aptamer to a change in the self-cleavage activity of a ribozyme.
source: Ribozyme switches, also known as aptazymes, are a special class of RNA switches that couple the binding of the ligand to an RNA aptamer to a change in the self-cleavage activity of a ribozyme (Win and Smolke, 2007).
evidence: This definitional claim is supported by a citation to Win and Smolke, 2007.

claim: The sTRSV hammerhead ribozyme self-cleaves when it adopts a specific tertiary conformation based on electrostatic interaction between nucleotides in two of its loops.
source: The sTRSV hammerhead ribozyme, one particular ribozyme, is a short sequence of RNA that self-cleaves when it adopts a specific tertiary conformation based on electrostatic interaction between nucleotides in two of its loops.
evidence: This is a mechanistic description of the sTRSV hammerhead ribozyme based on established knowledge.

claim: Changes in ribozyme cleavage activity result in changes to transcript stability and thus gene expression.
source: The ribozyme switch is integrated into a transcript such that changes in cleavage activity result in changes to transcript stability and thus gene expression (Figure 1A).
evidence: This claim describes the mechanism shown in Figure 1A.

claim: In tertiary-interaction ribozyme switches, one of the two loops is fixed as an RNA aptamer.
source: In tertiary-interaction ribozyme switches, one of the two loops is fixed as an RNA aptamer, and the sequence of the opposing loop (the variable loop) is selected so that the nucleotide interactions necessary for cleavage at physiological conditions occur in the basal state (or absence of ligand) (Townshend et al., 2015).
evidence: This design principle is supported by a citation to Townshend et al., 2015.

claim: A software tool was developed that computationally iterates through thousands of designs to identify a subset predicted to form secondary structures that may result in ligand-dependent transcription termination.
source: In one example, a software tool was developed that computationally iterates through thousands of designs to identify a subset predicted to form secondary structures that may result in ligand-dependent transcription termination (Domin et al., 2017).
evidence: This claim describes prior work supported by a citation to Domin et al., 2017.

claim: 17 switches were generated for three aptamers, and 12 of those (71%) exhibited significant changes in expression in the presence of the cognate ligand with activation ratios up to 4.
source: 17 switches were generated for three aptamers, and 12 of those (71%) exhibited significant changes in expression in the presence of the cognate ligand with activation ratios, defined as the ratio in gene-regulatory activities in the presence and absence of ligand, up to 4.
evidence: This claim reports experimental results from prior work (Domin et al., 2017).

claim: A biophysical model of ligand binding and RNA secondary structure conformation was developed to generate switches that occlude the ribosome binding site when the aptamer is not bound to the ligand.
source: In another example, a biophysical model of ligand binding and RNA secondary structure conformation was developed to generate switches that occlude the ribosome binding site when the aptamer is not bound to the ligand (Espah Borujeni et al., 2016).
evidence: This claim describes prior work supported by a citation to Espah Borujeni et al., 2016.

claim: The tool's predictions of activation ratio for 59 switch sequences fell within twofold of the measured activation ratio 63% of the time.
source: The tool's predictions of activation ratio for 59 switch sequences fell within twofold of the measured activation ratio 63% of the time, and select switches reached activation ratios of over 100.
evidence: This claim reports performance metrics from prior work (Espah Borujeni et al., 2016).

claim: Select switches reached activation ratios of over 100.
source: The tool's predictions of activation ratio for 59 switch sequences fell within twofold of the measured activation ratio 63% of the time, and select switches reached activation ratios of over 100.
evidence: This claim reports experimental results from prior work (Espah Borujeni et al., 2016).

claim: A computational method for switch design in mammalian systems leveraged a biophysical model to design inducible RNAi systems in HEK cells.
source: One computational method for switch design in mammalian systems leveraged a biophysical model of ligand binding and RNA secondary structure conformation to design inducible RNAi systems in HEK cells (Beisel et al., 2008).
evidence: This claim describes prior work supported by a citation to Beisel et al., 2008.

claim: The switches designed with this tool exhibited activation ratios of up to 5.
source: The switches designed with this tool exhibited activation ratios of up to 5.
evidence: This claim reports experimental results from prior work (Beisel et al., 2008).

claim: None of the computational design tools described to date are based on gene-regulatory platforms that function across a broad range of organisms.
source: However, none of the computational design tools described to date are based on gene-regulatory platforms that function across a broad range of organisms (Xiang et al., 2019).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Xiang et al., 2019.

claim: The ribozyme platform has been demonstrated in both bacterial and eukaryotic cells and across diverse applications.
source: We set out to fill this void by creating genetic switch design software for a ribozyme switch platform that has been demonstrated in both bacterial and eukaryotic cells and across diverse applications (Ausländer et al., 2010; Furukawa et al., 2014; Liang et al., 2012).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to three papers demonstrating the platform in different contexts.

claim: A convolutional neural network can learn how the sequence of a ribozyme determines its gene-regulatory activity with high accuracy for ribozymes with small loops (R2 = 0.91).
source: We demonstrated that a convolutional neural network (CNN) can learn how the sequence of a ribozyme determines its gene-regulatory activity with high accuracy for ribozymes with small loops (R2 = 0.91) and medium accuracy for ribozymes with an aptamer as one of the two loops (R2 = 0.28).
evidence: This claim reports the performance of the CNN model on experimental data.

claim: A convolutional neural network can learn how the sequence of a ribozyme determines its gene-regulatory activity with medium accuracy for ribozymes with an aptamer as one of the two loops (R2 = 0.28).
source: We demonstrated that a convolutional neural network (CNN) can learn how the sequence of a ribozyme determines its gene-regulatory activity with high accuracy for ribozymes with small loops (R2 = 0.91) and medium accuracy for ribozymes with an aptamer as one of the two loops (R2 = 0.28).
evidence: This claim reports the performance of the CNN model on experimental data.

claim: The model produced ribozyme switches with basal gene-regulatory activities lower than 30% of that from a nonfunctional ribozyme control for four of the five aptamers.
source: The model produced ribozyme switches with basal gene-regulatory activities lower than 30% of that from a nonfunctional ribozyme control (sufficient to enable activation ratios of at least 3) for four of the five aptamers and ribozyme switches that exhibit significant changes in gene-regulatory activity in response to the cognate ligand for all aptamers tested, proving that this model can be useful as a forward design tool for genetic switches.
evidence: This claim reports the experimental outcomes of applying the model to design switches.

claim: The model produced ribozyme switches that exhibit significant changes in gene-regulatory activity in response to the cognate ligand for all aptamers tested.
source: The model produced ribozyme switches with basal gene-regulatory activities lower than 30% of that from a nonfunctional ribozyme control (sufficient to enable activation ratios of at least 3) for four of the five aptamers and ribozyme switches that exhibit significant changes in gene-regulatory activity in response to the cognate ligand for all aptamers tested, proving that this model can be useful as a forward design tool for genetic switches.
evidence: This claim reports the experimental outcomes of applying the model to design switches.

claim: The first library was designed by randomizing the loop regions (loops I and II) with nucleotide sequences of lengths 5–10 on the base of sTRSV hammerhead ribozyme scaffold.
source: The first library was designed by randomizing the loop regions (loops I and II) with nucleotide sequences of lengths 5–10 on the base of sTRSV hammerhead ribozyme scaffold (Figure 2A).
evidence: This describes the experimental design of the first library, shown in Figure 2A.

claim: Libraries were cloned into the 3′ untranslated region (UTR) of a GFP expression cassette encoded on a low-copy plasmid.
source: Libraries were cloned into the 3′ untranslated region (UTR) of a GFP expression cassette encoded on a low-copy plasmid, such that ribozymes with high cleavage activities result in cells expressing low GFP levels.
evidence: This describes the experimental cloning strategy.

claim: Ribozymes with high cleavage activities result in cells expressing low GFP levels.
source: Libraries were cloned into the 3′ untranslated region (UTR) of a GFP expression cassette encoded on a low-copy plasmid, such that ribozymes with high cleavage activities result in cells expressing low GFP levels.
evidence: This describes the functional relationship between ribozyme cleavage and GFP expression in the experimental system.

claim: A constitutive mCherry expression cassette was included on the ribozyme library screening plasmid and used to normalize for intrinsic gene expression noise.
source: A constitutive mCherry expression cassette was included on the ribozyme library screening plasmid and used to normalize for intrinsic gene expression noise due to factors like cell cycle state and plasmid copy number (Liang et al., 2012).
evidence: This describes the experimental design for normalization, supported by a citation to Liang et al., 2012.

claim: FACS-Seq 1 consists of approximately 75,000 unique ribozyme sequences, for which at least 20 reads for each sequence were recorded.
source: FACS-Seq 1 consists of approximately 75,000 unique ribozyme sequences, for which at least 20 reads for each sequence were recorded.
evidence: This describes the size and coverage of the FACS-Seq 1 data set.

claim: 20,000 of these ribozymes have at least one loop with a length of ≥8.
source: 20,000 of these ribozymes have at least one loop with a length of ≥8, which is the size of the smallest aptamer loops.
evidence: This describes a subset of the FACS-Seq 1 data set.

claim: 48% of the sequences exhibit activity that is greater than half of that exhibited by a nonfunctional ribozyme.
source: 48% of the sequences exhibit activity that is greater than half of that exhibited by a nonfunctional ribozyme, and only 7% (1432 sequences) displayed activity near that of the native sTRSV hammerhead ribozyme.
evidence: This describes the distribution of activities in the FACS-Seq 1 data set.

claim: Only 7% (1432 sequences) displayed activity near that of the native sTRSV hammerhead ribozyme.
source: 48% of the sequences exhibit activity that is greater than half of that exhibited by a nonfunctional ribozyme, and only 7% (1432 sequences) displayed activity near that of the native sTRSV hammerhead ribozyme.
evidence: This describes the distribution of activities in the FACS-Seq 1 data set.

claim: Most of the possible nucleotide sequence combinations for loops I and II do not result in functional nucleotide interactions that support high cleavage activity at physiological conditions.
source: The activity data indicates that most of the possible nucleotide sequence combinations for loops I and II do not result in functional nucleotide interactions that support high cleavage activity at physiological conditions.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the activity distribution data from FACS-Seq 1.

claim: The second library was designed with one of the loops harboring a randomized sequence of larger length (N9–N13) and the other loop harboring a shorter randomized sequence (N5–N7).
source: The library was designed with one of the loops (loop I or II) harboring a randomized sequence of larger length (N9–N13) and the other loop (loop II or I, respectively) harboring a shorter randomized sequence (N5–N7).
evidence: This describes the experimental design of the second library.

claim: FACS-Seq 2 consists of approximately 61,000 unique ribozyme sequences.
source: FACS-Seq 2 consists of approximately 61,000 unique ribozyme sequences.
evidence: This describes the size of the FACS-Seq 2 data set.

claim: FACS-Seq 3 consists of approximately 9000 unique ribozyme sequences.
source: FACS-Seq 3 consists of approximately 9000 unique ribozyme sequences.
evidence: This describes the size of the FACS-Seq 3 data set.

claim: Through the design and testing of multiple ribozyme libraries, roughly 150,000 unique ribozyme sequences were characterized.
source: Through the design and testing of multiple ribozyme libraries, we generated individual measurements of gene-regulatory activities for roughly 150,000 unique ribozyme sequences (10,000 of which exhibit gene-regulatory activities close to that of the native ribozyme), achieving a data set with a broad range of activities.
evidence: This summarizes the total size of the training data set generated.

claim: 10,000 ribozyme sequences exhibit gene-regulatory activities close to that of the native ribozyme.
source: Through the design and testing of multiple ribozyme libraries, we generated individual measurements of gene-regulatory activities for roughly 150,000 unique ribozyme sequences (10,000 of which exhibit gene-regulatory activities close to that of the native ribozyme), achieving a data set with a broad range of activities.
evidence: This describes a subset of the training data set with low gene-regulatory activities.

claim: Approximately 60,000 of the ribozymes in the characterized library have a loop with length >8.
source: Approximately 60,000 of the ribozymes in the characterized library have a loop with length >8, and 4,000 of these large-loop sequences displayed near-native gene-regulatory activity.
evidence: This describes a subset of the training data set with larger loops.

claim: 4,000 large-loop sequences displayed near-native gene-regulatory activity.
source: Approximately 60,000 of the ribozymes in the characterized library have a loop with length >8, and 4,000 of these large-loop sequences displayed near-native gene-regulatory activity.
evidence: This describes a subset of the training data set with large loops and low gene-regulatory activities.

claim: The neural network model was more accurate than the lasso model in predicting activities of N4N4 ribozymes (R2 = 0.91 vs. R2 = 0.82).
source: Both models were able to predict the activities in the simulated test subset (25% of the constructed training set) with high accuracy; however, the neural network (R2 = 0.91) was more accurate than the lasso algorithm (R2 = 0.82). (Figure 4B).
evidence: This compares the performance of two models on test data, shown in Figure 4B.

claim: The neural network model generated an R2 value of 0.27 for predicting theophylline ribozyme activities, which was much higher than the lasso model's R2 value of 0.08.
source: Both models were less accurate in predicting the activities of more complex ribozyme sequences than when predicting the activities of N4N4 ribozymes; however, the neural network model generated an R2 value that was much higher than the R2 value produced by the lasso model (0.27 vs 0.08).
evidence: This compares the performance of two models on theophylline ribozyme test data.

claim: The 10 ribozymes with the lowest neural network-predicted activities had a mean log10(GFP/mCherry) value of –1.04.
source: The 10 ribozymes with the lowest neural network-predicted activities had a mean log10(GFP/mCherry) value of –1.04, while the best lasso-predicted ribozymes had a mean log10(GFP/mCherry) value of –0.69.
evidence: This reports the performance of the neural network model in identifying low-activity ribozymes.

claim: The best lasso-predicted ribozymes had a mean log10(GFP/mCherry) value of –0.69.
source: The 10 ribozymes with the lowest neural network-predicted activities had a mean log10(GFP/mCherry) value of –1.04, while the best lasso-predicted ribozymes had a mean log10(GFP/mCherry) value of –0.69.
evidence: This reports the performance of the lasso model in identifying low-activity ribozymes.

claim: For each test segment of ribozymes with a shared structure, the neural network's predictions had an R2 value an average of 0.18 greater than the predictions from the lasso model.
source: For each test segment of ribozymes with a shared structure, the neural network's predictions had an R2 value an average of 0.18 greater than the predictions from the lasso model (Figure 4F).
evidence: This compares the robustness of the two models across different structural segments, shown in Figure 4F.

claim: The segments where the stem length was different than the standard ribozyme stem had an even greater difference in R2 (0.53).
source: Furthermore, the neural network's R2 values were higher than the lasso model for every single structural segment, and the segments where the stem length was different than the standard ribozyme stem had an even greater difference in R2 (0.53).
evidence: This reports the performance difference between models on ribozymes with non-standard stem lengths.

claim: The designed folinic acid library had a mean gene-regulatory activity value of log10(GFP/mCherry) = –0.36 vs. 0.62 for the random library.
source: The designed library had a mean gene-regulatory activity value of log10(GFP/mCherry) = –0.36 vs. 0.62 for the random library.
evidence: This reports the experimental comparison of designed vs. random libraries for folinic acid.

claim: The fraction of ribozymes in the designed folinic acid library with low gene-regulatory activity was 77% vs. 3% for the random library.
source: The fraction of ribozymes in the designed library with low gene-regulatory activity was 77% vs. 3% for the random library.
evidence: This reports the experimental comparison of designed vs. random libraries for folinic acid.

claim: The rank-sum test determined that the folinic acid designed and random libraries had a 0.0% probability (p=1.2 × 10–91) of coming from the same distribution.
source: Finally, the results of the rank-sum test determined that the two libraries had a 0.0% probability (p=1.2 × 10–91) of coming from the same distribution.
evidence: This reports the statistical analysis of the folinic acid library comparison.

claim: The designed theophylline library had a mean gene-regulatory activity value of 0.31 vs. 0.55 for the random library.
source: Specifically, the designed libraries had mean gene-regulatory activity values of 0.31 (theophylline), 0.30 (tetracycline), and 0.38 (chloramphenicol) vs. 0.55, 0.44, and 0.49, respectively, for the corresponding random libraries.
evidence: This reports the experimental comparison of designed vs. random libraries for theophylline.

claim: The designed tetracycline library had a mean gene-regulatory activity value of 0.30 vs. 0.44 for the random library.
source: Specifically, the designed libraries had mean gene-regulatory activity values of 0.31 (theophylline), 0.30 (tetracycline), and 0.38 (chloramphenicol) vs. 0.55, 0.44, and 0.49, respectively, for the corresponding random libraries.
evidence: This reports the experimental comparison of designed vs. random libraries for tetracycline.

claim: The designed chloramphenicol library had a mean gene-regulatory activity value of 0.38 vs. 0.49 for the random library.
source: Specifically, the designed libraries had mean gene-regulatory activity values of 0.31 (theophylline), 0.30 (tetracycline), and 0.38 (chloramphenicol) vs. 0.55, 0.44, and 0.49, respectively, for the corresponding random libraries.
evidence: This reports the experimental comparison of designed vs. random libraries for chloramphenicol.

claim: The fraction of ribozymes in the designed theophylline library with low gene-regulatory activity was 15% vs. 2% for the random library.
source: The fraction of ribozymes in the designed libraries with low gene-regulatory activity was 15% (theophylline), 8% (tetracycline), and 0.6% (chloramphenicol) vs. 2%, 1%, and 0.1%, respectively, for the corresponding random libraries.
evidence: This reports the experimental comparison of designed vs. random libraries for theophylline.

claim: The fraction of ribozymes in the designed tetracycline library with low gene-regulatory activity was 8% vs. 1% for the random library.
source: The fraction of ribozymes in the designed libraries with low gene-regulatory activity was 15% (theophylline), 8% (tetracycline), and 0.6% (chloramphenicol) vs. 2%, 1%, and 0.1%, respectively, for the corresponding random libraries.
evidence: This reports the experimental comparison of designed vs. random libraries for tetracycline.

claim: The fraction of ribozymes in the designed chloramphenicol library with low gene-regulatory activity was 0.6% vs. 0.1% for the random library.
source: The fraction of ribozymes in the designed libraries with low gene-regulatory activity was 15% (theophylline), 8% (tetracycline), and 0.6% (chloramphenicol) vs. 2%, 1%, and 0.1%, respectively, for the corresponding random libraries.
evidence: This reports the experimental comparison of designed vs. random libraries for chloramphenicol.

claim: The designed neomycin library had a mean gene-regulatory activity value of log10(GFP/mCherry) = 0.64 vs. 0.73 for the random library.
source: The designed neomycin aptamer library had a mean gene-regulatory activity value of log10(GFP/mCherry) = 0.64 vs. 0.73 for the random library.
evidence: This reports the experimental comparison of designed vs. random libraries for neomycin.

claim: The fraction of ribozymes in the designed neomycin library with low gene-regulatory activity was 0% vs. 0.01% for the random library.
source: However, the fraction of ribozymes in the designed library with low gene-regulatory activity was 0% vs. 0.01% for the random library.
evidence: This reports the experimental comparison of designed vs. random libraries for neomycin.

claim: The top 15 ribozymes designed with the folinic acid aptamer exhibited very low basal gene-regulatory activities, with a median of 3.2% of the nonfunctional ribozyme.
source: Similar to the aptamer's designed library, the top 15 ribozymes designed with the folinic acid aptamer exhibited very low basal gene-regulatory activities, with a median of 3.2% of the nonfunctional ribozyme and a very low interquartile range (the difference between the 75th and 25th percentiles) of 1.8% (Figure 6A).
evidence: This reports the experimental characterization of top folinic acid designs, shown in Figure 6A.

claim: In the presence of high concentrations of folinic acid, the median activity increased to 4.7%, resulting in a median activation ratio of 1.5.
source: In the presence of high concentrations of folinic acid, the median activity increased to 4.7%, resulting in a median activation ratio of 1.5 (Figure 6B).
evidence: This reports the experimental characterization of top folinic acid designs in the presence of ligand, shown in Figure 6B.

claim: The top three performing folinic acid ribozymes exhibited activation ratios spanning 2.2–2.9.
source: The top three performing ribozymes exhibited activation ratios spanning 2.2–2.9 (Figure 6C).
evidence: This reports the experimental characterization of the best folinic acid designs, shown in Figure 6C.

claim: The top 15 ribozymes designed with the tetracycline aptamer exhibited low basal gene-regulatory activities, with a median of 26.3% of the nonfunctional ribozyme.
source: The top 15 ribozymes designed with the tetracycline aptamer exhibited low basal gene-regulatory activities, with a median of 26.3% of the nonfunctional ribozyme.
evidence: This reports the experimental characterization of top tetracycline designs.

claim: In the presence of high concentrations of tetracycline, the median activity increased to 75.6%, resulting in a median activation ratio of 2.8.
source: In the presence of high concentrations of tetracycline, the median activity increased to 75.6%, resulting in a median activation ratio of 2.8.
evidence: This reports the experimental characterization of top tetracycline designs in the presence of ligand.

claim: The top three performing tetracycline ribozymes exhibited activation ratios spanning 4.5–5.8.
source: The top three performing ribozymes exhibited activation ratios spanning 4.5–5.8, and all exhibited low basal gene-regulatory activities (spanning 10.7–14.3%).
evidence: This reports the experimental characterization of the best tetracycline designs.

claim: The top 15 ribozymes designed with the chloramphenicol aptamer exhibited low basal gene-regulatory activity with a median of 41.9% of the nonfunctional ribozyme.
source: The top 15 ribozymes designed with the chloramphenicol aptamer exhibited low basal gene-regulatory activity with a median of 41.9% of the nonfunctional ribozyme, similar to that of the ribozymes designed with the tetracycline aptamer.
evidence: This reports the experimental characterization of top chloramphenicol designs.

claim: The median gene-regulatory activity for chloramphenicol ribozymes only increases slightly to 46.1% in the presence of high concentrations of chloramphenicol, resulting in a median activation ratio of 1.1.
source: Unlike the tetracycline-responsive ribozymes, the median gene-regulatory activity only increases slightly to 46.1% in the presence of high concentrations of chloramphenicol, resulting in a median activation ratio of 1.1.
evidence: This reports the experimental characterization of top chloramphenicol designs in the presence of ligand.

claim: The top 15 ribozymes designed with the theophylline aptamer exhibited high gene-regulatory activities in the absence of theophylline, with a median of 77.0% of the nonfunctional ribozyme.
source: Although the model produced several ribozymes with low gene-regulatory activities, on average the ribozymes among the predicted top 15 sequences exhibited high gene-regulatory activities in the absence of theophylline, with a median of 77.0% of the nonfunctional ribozyme.
evidence: This reports the experimental characterization of top theophylline designs.

claim: In the presence of high concentrations of theophylline, the median activity increased to 80.6%, resulting in a median activation ratio of 1.2.
source: In the presence of high concentrations of theophylline, the median activity increased to 80.6%, resulting in a median activation ratio of 1.2.
evidence: This reports the experimental characterization of top theophylline designs in the presence of ligand.

claim: The top three performing theophylline ribozyme switches exhibited basal gene-regulatory activities as low as 12.7% and activation ratios up to 4.0.
source: However, due to the variability in activities across the top 15 predicted sequences, the top three performing ribozyme switches exhibited basal gene-regulatory activities as low as 12.7% and activation ratios up to 4.0.
evidence: This reports the experimental characterization of the best theophylline designs.

claim: The top 15 ribozymes designed with the neomycin aptamer did not exhibit low gene-regulatory activities, with a median of 72.5% of the nonfunctional ribozyme.
source: Similar to the aptamer's designed library, the top 15 ribozymes designed with the neomycin aptamer did not exhibit low gene-regulatory activities, with a median of 72.5% of the nonfunctional ribozyme.
evidence: This reports the experimental characterization of top neomycin designs.

claim: In the presence of neomycin, a substantial increase in activities was observed, with a median of 98.7%, resulting in a median activation ratio of 1.4.
source: Despite the high gene-regulatory activities in the absence of ligand, a substantial increase in activities was observed in the presence of neomycin, with a median of 98.7%, resulting in a median activation ratio of 1.4.
evidence: This reports the experimental characterization of top neomycin designs in the presence of ligand.

claim: The top three performing neomycin sequences exhibited basal gene-regulatory activities as low as 44.3% and activation ratios up to 2.0.
source: The top three performing sequences exhibited basal gene-regulatory activities as low as 44.3% and activation ratios up to 2.0, thus reaching near the theoretical upper limit of gene-regulatory activity in the presence of ligand (i.e., 100%).
evidence: This reports the experimental characterization of the best neomycin designs.

claim: 1.5% of the variable loop sequences in the designed libraries are generally favored by the model independent of the aptamer sequence.
source: The results of this analysis indicate that 1.5% of the variable loop sequences in the designed libraries are generally favored by the model independent of the aptamer sequence.
evidence: This reports the analysis of shared sequences across designed libraries.

claim: 4 sequences were in every aptamer's designed library and a further 11 sequences were in four of the five libraries.
source: Specifically, 4 sequences were in every aptamer's designed library (of 200 sequences) and a further 11 sequences were in four of the five libraries.
evidence: This reports the analysis of shared sequences across designed libraries.

claim: These sequences share a 5-nucleotide motif on loop II (UGGAG) that the model deemed generally favorable for cleavage.
source: These sequences share a 5-nucleotide motif on loop II (UGGAG) that the model deemed generally favorable for cleavage (Figure 7B).
evidence: This reports the identification of a conserved motif in the model predictions, shown in Figure 7B.

claim: Sequences with the UGGAG motif displayed a mean log10(GFP/mCherry) value of –0.27 vs. a mean log10(GFP/mCherry) value of 0.02 for ribozymes with random loop sequences.
source: Sequences with this motif displayed a mean log10(GFP/mCherry) value of –0.27 vs. a mean log10(GFP/mCherry) value of 0.02 for ribozymes with random loop sequences.
evidence: This reports the experimental validation of the UGGAG motif in the training data.

claim: 75% of the folinic acid designs have the aptamer on loop II.

claim: RNAstructure has good accuracy, with a correlation between predicted and known RNA structures among the highest of all RNA secondary structure prediction methods.
source: We used the RNA secondary structure prediction software RNAstructure (Reuter and Mathews, 2010) for the computational folding of ribozymes as it has good accuracy, with a correlation between predicted and known RNA structures among the highest of all RNA secondary structure prediction methods (Puton et al., 2013), on short RNA sequences and can fold several sequences of ribozyme length (roughly 100 nucleotides) per second on a standard desktop computer.
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Puton et al., 2013.

claim: The ribozyme switch platform has been demonstrated in mammalian cells.
source: We set out to fill this void by creating genetic switch design software for a ribozyme switch platform that has been demonstrated in both bacterial and eukaryotic cells and across diverse applications (Ausländer et al., 2010; Furukawa et al., 2014; Liang et al., 2012).
evidence: The text states the platform works in eukaryotic cells, and mammalian cells are a type of eukaryotic cell, supported by the citations.

claim: The accuracy of the neural network model declines rapidly as the structure of ribozymes in the training set differs from the structure of the ribozymes whose gene-regulatory activity the model is predicting.
source: It is particularly important to note that the accuracy of the neural network model declines rapidly as the structure of ribozymes in the training set differs from the structure of the ribozymes whose gene-regulatory activity the model is predicting (Figure 4—figure supplement 3C).

claim: Certain ligands may not be well-suited to being used as effectors of genetic switches used in cells due to cellular toxicity or membrane permeability of the ligand.
source: Certain ligands may not be well-suited to being used as effectors of genetic switches used in cells, for example, due to cellular toxicity or membrane permeability of the ligand (Xiang et al., 2019).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Xiang et al., 2019.

claim: The greater success of the tetracycline-responsive ribozymes as genetic switches relative to the folinic acid-responsive ribozymes likely results from the ability of tetracycline to more efficiently cross the cell membrane.
source: The greater success of the tetracycline-responsive ribozymes as genetic switches relative to the folinic acid-responsive ribozymes likely results from particular features of the ligand-aptamer pair, including the ability of tetracycline to more efficiently cross the cell membrane (Argast and Beck, 1984).
evidence: This interpretation is supported by a citation to Argast and Beck, 1984.

claim: Folinic acid does not cross the cell membrane efficiently.
source: Given the relatively high affinity of the aptamer to its ligand (Chang, 2014), these results imply that folinic acid does not cross the cell membrane efficiently, thus resulting in very low intracellular concentrations (Xiang et al., 2019; Niethammer and Kleihauer, 1974), or does not bind to the aptamer in a way that effectively disrupts ribozyme cleavage.
evidence: This interpretation is supported by citations to Xiang et al., 2019 and Niethammer and Kleihauer, 1974.

claim: Chloramphenicol does not cross the yeast membrane efficiently.
source: Similar to the folinic acid ligand-aptamer pair, these results imply that chloramphenicol does not cross the yeast membrane efficiently (Abdel-Sayed, 1987), its toxicity at high concentrations limits the intracellular concentrations attainable, or it does not bind to the aptamer in a way that effectively disrupts ribozyme cleavage.
evidence: This interpretation is supported by a citation to Abdel-Sayed, 1987.

claim: Evidence from crystal structures for the native hammerhead ribozyme supports the assumption of the nucleotides being arranged in two thin opposing planes.
source: Evidence from crystal structures for the native hammerhead ribozyme supports this assumption of the nucleotides being arranged in two thin opposing planes (Chi et al., 2008).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Chi et al., 2008.
